messages.author: a523f4070ecfcf39
messages.subject: R bug tickled via plyr?
parts:
This first snippet demonstrates tickling the bug via plyr.  I can get R to segfault pretty reliably if I use transform instead of mutate in the dlply below.

# Construct a data frame with 10,000 distinct groups, each 10 elements long,
# where a_number is always NA.  (If a_number is not always NA, there is no problem). 
library(plyr)
ngroups=10000
tst2<-data.frame(factor1=rep(1:ngroups,10), a_number=NA)
head(tst2)
summary(tst2)
sav <- dlply(tst2, "factor1",
             mutate,  # with mutate, no segfaults
             #transform,   # with transform, R will sometimes segfault in the sapply() below
             min=min(a_number, na.rm=TRUE))

# Some of the results aren't data frames!  The results are different each time.
which(sapply(sav, class) != "data.frame")


But I can't pare down the example to something simpler that doesn't use plyr.  This loop always runs to completion.

# Never breaks
foo<-data.frame(factor1="A",a_number=rep(NA,10))
for(idx in 1:100000) {
  res<-transform(foo, min=min(a_number,na.rm=TRUE))
  if (class(res) != "data.frame") {
    print("Not a data.frame!!!")
    break
  }
}


Is this a known problem?  Is this something I should file in the main R bugzilla?  In my real code, I am able to work around this issue using summarize() and merging the results back into the larger data frame, so I think the problem has to do with how mutate() and transform() work.

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: R bug tickled via plyr?
parts:
Thanks John, this is super helpful. I've managed to reduce the problem
to an error in loop_apply:

library(plyr)
ngroups <- 10000
tst2 <- data.frame(factor1 = rep(1:ngroups, 10), a_number = NA)

pieces <- split(tst2, tst2$factor1)

sav <- plyr:::loop_apply(length(pieces), function(i) {
piece <- pieces[[i]]
transform(piece, min = min(a_number, na.rm = TRUE))
})

df <- vapply(sav, is.data.frame, logical(1))
which(!df)

loop_apply() is an internal C++ function:

List loop_apply(int n, Function f) {
List out(n);

for(int i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
out[i] = f(i + 1);
}

return out;
}

That's so simple I don't think I've made an error, so I suspect it's a
problem with PROTECTion in the underlying Rcpp code. For now, I've
reverted to the old C implementation of this function and it fixes the
problem. You can try it out with
devtools::install_github("hadley/plyr")

Hadley

messages.author: 8129606756857cb3
messages.subject: Re: R bug tickled via plyr?
parts:
I looked into this a little bit, and here's my guess -- the Rcpp `Function` class does not properly protect the 'language' objects used when invoking the function.

For example, look here:

https://github.com/RcppCore/Rcpp/blob/master/inst/include/Rcpp/Function.h#L77-L79

An `Rcpp_eval` is called with the unprotected return of `Rf_lang1`. This effectively means that the language object that was used for the function evaluation could be cleaned up, and so any function that tries to do introspection on the arguments passed (`match.call()` and friends) may break.

This same template is used e.g. here:

https://github.com/RcppCore/Rcpp/blob/master/inst/include/Rcpp/generated/Function__operator.h#L33-L36

I think this gets touched by the `eval(substitute(list(...)))` call in `transform.data.frame`, hence the bug seen. And since cleaning up of those nodes is somewhat non-deterministic this bug will be quite hard to repro.

So I believe the solution is to, on the Rcpp side, ensure those `language` objects generated for the evaluation should be protected before evaluating the function.

(Somewhat ironically, this issue is pointed out in adv-r, in a section I contributed parts to: http://adv-r.had.co.nz/C-interface.html#c-pairlists; so it's a little sad that a bug like that languished in Rcpp!)
